subject.title: feat(nodes): continue Claude catalog sessions on paired nodes via streaming CLI agent runs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this paired-node native agent-run protocol and configuration in core now, and if so should resolveChildProcessInvocation become a supported public Plugin SDK API?
rationale: This introduces sensitive native execution, new gateway protocol messages, a new configuration surface, and an external SDK commitment; repository policy treats each as compatibility-sensitive and the permanent contract cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Land the narrowed contract
options.body: Keep the opt-in feature, move the spawn helper back behind a core-internal boundary, obtain real paired-node proof, and land only the intentionally additive protocol and runtime seams.

options.title: Approve the SDK API
options.body: Explicitly adopt resolveChildProcessInvocation as a supported plugin contract with public documentation, compatibility tests, and a stated long-term ownership boundary.

options.title: Defer node agent runs
options.body: Pause this PR until a broader generic node-agent execution contract is designed rather than committing the Claude-specific v1 protocol now.

recommendation.title: Land the narrowed contract
recommendation.body: Keep the opt-in feature, move the spawn helper back behind a core-internal boundary, obtain real paired-node proof, and land only the intentionally additive protocol and runtime seams.

likelyOwner.reason: The available merged history and canonical issue connect this person most directly to CLI-backend direction and the proposed paired-node design.
